title: Serre vanishing for a proper morphism
statement: Let $A$ be Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], let $\mathcal F$ be a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent], and let $\mathcal L$ be an ample [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module]. There exists $n_0\ge0$ such that $H^p(X,\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes n})=0$ [pqf-def-cohomology] for every $p>0$ and $n\ge n_0$; the tensor product and the tensor power are those of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product].

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 02O1 (coherent-lemma-kill-by-twisting), specialized to an affine base; Morphisms Lemma 01VK (morphisms-lemma-ample-over-affine) identifies absolute and relative ampleness over an affine base.

proof.text: *Noetherian setting.* $A$ is Noetherian, so $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ is locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] (covered by the single affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A$ with Noetherian ring of sections) and quasi-compact [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact] (iii), i.e. a Noetherian scheme. The proper morphism $f$ is of finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism], so $X$ is Noetherian, in particular locally Noetherian, by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. For $N\ge0$ the scheme $P_N=\operatorname{Proj}(A[x_0,\dots,x_N])$ [def-pc-proj] is covered by the standard opens $D_+(x_k)=\operatorname{Spec}(A[x_0,\dots,x_N]_{(x_k)})$, and $A[x_0,\dots,x_N]_{(x_k)}=A[x_0/x_k,\dots,x_N/x_k]$ is a finitely generated $A$-algebra, hence Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]; so $P_N$ is locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth].

source.place: Lemma 0B5T, proof (Noetherian hypotheses implicit in the use of Lemma 01YS and 087T)

proof.text: *A power of $\mathcal L$ comes from $\mathcal O(1)$ along an immersion.* $f$ is of finite type, in particular locally of finite type, and $\mathcal L$ is ample on $X$. By [lem-weil-pbc-ample-very-ample-immersion-affine-base] there are $d\ge1$, $N\ge0$, an immersion $i:X\to P:=P_N$ with $q\circ i=f$ ($q:P\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ the structure morphism) and an isomorphism $\mathcal L^{\otimes d}\cong i^*\mathcal O_P(1)$, with $\mathcal O_P(1)$ the twisting module of [def-pc-projective-space-twist]. Fix them and write $\mathcal M=i^*\mathcal O_P(1)$.

*$i$ is a closed immersion.* $q$ is separated [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-proj-separated] and $q\circ i=f$ is proper, so $i$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-over-separated]. A proper immersion is a closed immersion [lem-weil-pbc-proper-immersion-closed]. So $i:X\to P$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] of locally Noetherian schemes (Step 1).

source.place: Lemma 0B5T, proof ('Since X is proper over R the morphism i is a closed immersion', Morphisms Lemma 01W6)

proof.text: *The twists $\mathcal G_r$ and their twists are coherent.* For $r\in\{0,\dots,d-1\}$ and $t\ge0$ put $\mathcal G_{r,t}=\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes r}\otimes\mathcal M^{\otimes t}$ and $\mathcal G_r=\mathcal G_{r,0}=\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes r}$ (tensor products and powers of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]). $\mathcal L$ and $\mathcal M$ are invertible ($\mathcal M$ because it is isomorphic to the invertible $\mathcal L^{\otimes d}$): every point of $X$ has an open neighbourhood $W$ on which $\mathcal L|_W\cong\mathcal O_W$ and $\mathcal M|_W\cong\mathcal O_W$ [def-sc-invertible-module] (intersect the two trivializing neighbourhoods), and there $\mathcal G_{r,t}|_W\cong\mathcal F|_W\otimes\mathcal O_W\otimes\dots\otimes\mathcal O_W\cong\mathcal F|_W$. Since $\mathcal F$ is coherent on the locally Noetherian $X$, it is quasi-coherent of finite type by [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]; both properties are local [pqf-def-coherent], so $\mathcal G_{r,t}$ is quasi-coherent of finite type, hence coherent by [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth] again. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-coherent-equivalence] (1), applied to the closed immersion $i$ of locally Noetherian schemes (Step 3), $i_*\mathcal G_r$ and every $i_*\mathcal G_{r,t}$ are coherent $\mathcal O_P$-modules.

source.place: Lemma 0B5T, proof ('if G is coherent, then i_*G is coherent as well', Lemma 087T)

proof.text: *Projection formula: $i_*\mathcal G_{r,t}\cong i_*\mathcal G_r\otimes\mathcal O_P(t)$ for all $t\ge0$.* Induction on $t$. For $t=0$: $\mathcal O_P(0)$ is glued from the $\mathcal O_{U_k}e^{(0)}_k$ with transitions $e^{(0)}_k=(x_k/x_j)^0e^{(0)}_j=e^{(0)}_j$ [def-pc-projective-space-twist], so $e^{(0)}_k\mapsto1$ defines $\mathcal O_P(0)\cong\mathcal O_P$, and $i_*\mathcal G_r\otimes\mathcal O_P\cong i_*\mathcal G_r$. For $t\ge1$: $\mathcal G_{r,t}\cong\mathcal G_{r,t-1}\otimes i^*\mathcal O_P(1)$ by associativity of the tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]; $\mathcal G_{r,t-1}$ is coherent (Step 4) and $\mathcal O_P(1)$ is invertible on $P$ [def-pc-projective-space-twist], so the projection formula of [lem-pc-closed-immersion-coherent-cohomology] (closed immersion of locally Noetherian schemes, Steps 1 and 3) gives $i_*\mathcal G_{r,t}\cong i_*(\mathcal G_{r,t-1}\otimes i^*\mathcal O_P(1))\cong i_*\mathcal G_{r,t-1}\otimes\mathcal O_P(1)$. By the induction hypothesis and [lem-pc-twist-tensor] ($\mathcal O_P(t-1)\otimes\mathcal O_P(1)\cong\mathcal O_P(t)$), this is $\cong i_*\mathcal G_r\otimes\mathcal O_P(t-1)\otimes\mathcal O_P(1)\cong i_*\mathcal G_r\otimes\mathcal O_P(t)=(i_*\mathcal G_r)(t)$.

source.place: Lemma 0B5T, proof of (4) (projection formula, Cohomology Lemma 01E8)

proof.text: *Cohomology on $X$ is cohomology on $P$.* For $n=td+r$ with $t\ge0$, $0\le r<d$: $\mathcal L^{\otimes n}\cong\mathcal L^{\otimes r}\otimes(\mathcal L^{\otimes d})^{\otimes t}\cong\mathcal L^{\otimes r}\otimes\mathcal M^{\otimes t}$ (associativity and commutativity of $\otimes$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and the isomorphism $\mathcal L^{\otimes d}\cong\mathcal M$ of Step 2), so $\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes n}\cong\mathcal G_{r,t}$; as $H^p(X,-)$ is a functor [pqf-def-cohomology], $H^p(X,\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes n})\cong H^p(X,\mathcal G_{r,t})$. The closed immersion $i$ is an affine morphism and $\mathcal G_{r,t}$ is quasi-coherent (Step 4), so the edge map of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-cohomology-edge] is an isomorphism $H^p(P,i_*\mathcal G_{r,t})\cong H^p(X,\mathcal G_{r,t})$. With Step 5: $H^p(X,\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes(td+r)})\cong H^p(P,(i_*\mathcal G_r)(t))$ for every $p\ge0$, $t\ge0$, $0\le r<d$.

source.place: Lemma 0B5T, proof ('H^i(X,G) = H^i(P^n_R, i_*G) for any quasi-coherent G', Lemma 089W and Morphisms Lemma 01SE) and proof of (4)

proof.text: *Serre vanishing on $P$ and the bound $n_0$.* For each $r\in\{0,\dots,d-1\}$, $i_*\mathcal G_r$ is a coherent module on $P=\mathbf P^N_A$ with $A$ Noetherian (Step 4), so [lem-pc-projective-space-serre-vanishing] gives $t_r\ge0$ with $H^p(P,(i_*\mathcal G_r)(t))=0$ for all $t\ge t_r$ and $p>0$ (there $\mathcal H(t)=\mathcal H\otimes\mathcal O_P(t)$). Put $T=\max_rt_r$ and $n_0=dT$. If $n\ge n_0$, division with remainder writes $n=td+r$ with $0\le r<d$ and $t=\lfloor n/d\rfloor\ge T\ge t_r$, so by Step 6 $H^p(X,\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes n})\cong H^p(P,(i_*\mathcal G_r)(t))=0$ for every $p>0$. Since there are only finitely many residues $r$, this proves the lemma.
